summary: Midday dedicated throughput drift triggered by sidecar sample-upload burst and transient GPU attach failures
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lexicon AI reported a gradual but persistent drop in dedicated pool throughput during midday (11:30–12:45 UTC) on 2026-03-10. P95/P99 token throughput and attach success rate decreased while error rates for short-lived GPU attach timeouts rose. Impacted traffic is routed to the customer's reserved GPU pool (dedicated).

Impact:
- Customer observed ~30–60% throughput degradation for batched routes and elevated p99 latency for short streaming requests.
- Some requests returned 503/504 during attach attempts; others experienced long queueing before serving.
- Revenue-impacting for high-throughput inference routes during the window.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved) pool: prod, us-east region, GPU fleet heterogeneous (A100/RTX6000 mix), customer's tenant pinned to model redwood-7b-instruct v2026-02-21.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Normal traffic baseline at 11:20 UTC.
2) Sidecar sample-upload process from a teammate application (different tenant) starts a burst of high-frequency telemetry/sample uploads at ~11:30 UTC.
3) Over ~5–10 minutes memory/IO on nodes hosting sidecar agents spikes; allocator begins to report attach slowdowns.
4) Dedicated pool autoscaler does not immediately add GPUs (policy cooldown), causing transient attach failures and batch serialization.
5) Throughput drifts downward until burst subsides (around 12:45 UTC).

Observed behavior:
- Attach timeout spikes in logs: attach_timeouts increased from baseline 0.1% to 6.3% during the window.
- GPU attach latency histogram shifted right with p95 moving from ~120ms to ~1.2s.
- Sidecar ingress I/O on affected hosts saturated NIC bond intermittently.
- Prefetch/KV cache hit-rates decreased for tenants sharing those hosts causing more work per request.

Expected behavior:
- Sidecar telemetry uploads should be rate-limited to avoid impacting allocator/attach paths for dedicated pools.
- Autoscaler should react within policy bounds to maintain attach success SLA or move traffic via fallback routing earlier.

Key logs/links:
- Kibana: https://kibana.redwood.ai/app/discover#/view/throughput-drift-us-east?query=SUP-515151
- Traces: https://tracing.redwood.ai/trace/0d5a6b2f
- Dedicated autoscaler events timeline: https://console.redwood.ai/dedicated/pools/lexicon-us-east/events

Notes: Customer-side instrumentation shows sample-upload spikes originating from Lexicon's analytics sidecar, but uploads were higher than expected for a non-production job.
comments: 2026-03-10 12:05 - Asha Mehta (Support): Logged initial report from Lexicon AI. Provided temporary workaround suggestion to throttle sample uploads from their analytics sidecar and requested logs. SLA flagged P1.

2026-03-10 12:28 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Correlated attach timeouts to NIC/IO saturation on 3 hosts in us-east cluster. Opening host-level investigation; tentative hypothesis: sidecar upload flood causing host egress/backpressure and delaying CUDA driver handshake paths.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Priya Nair (Serving Runtime): Observed increased prefetch misses and KV cache churn on affected nodes that were colocated with heavy sidecar upload traffic. Suggest limiting sidecar max-concurrency and adding egress QoS to sidecar process.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Lexicon AI (Customer): We've limited sample uploads overnight and saw throughput return to baseline. Can you confirm what internal mitigations are planned to avoid recurrence?

2026-03-11 11:00 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed we reproduced noisy-sidecar upload locally. Created hotfix to apply host-level traffic shaping for sidecar processes and a scheduler change to avoid placing high-ingress sidecars on GPU host network paths. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sidecar-agent/pull/4321

2026-03-12 16:20 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Rolled out staged traffic-shaping and scheduler rule to us-east canary (10% of hosts). Initial telemetry shows attach_timeouts reduced to baseline and throughput recovered. Planning full roll-out tomorrow 2026-03-13.
2026-03-13 09:48 - Support (Asha Mehta): Notified customer Lexicon AI of mitigation rollout and received confirmation that scheduled batch validation jobs will be reconfigured to lower concurrency.
investigation_notes: Telemetry snapshot shows correlation between sidecar egress bursts and increased kernel-level overhead on NIC drivers; hosts showed elevated rx_dropped and tx_queue length spikes.

Allocators reported attach handshake retries with underlying error path: CUDA driver delayed responses / epoll wake latency increased.
Relevant logs: /var/log/redwood/attach/attach-2026-03-10.log lines 1024-1210
Reproduced locally with a synthetic sidecar uploader at 500 rps and confirmed that NVME + NIC saturation path increases p95 attach latency by ~8x on mixed A100/RTX hosts.
Autoscaler policy note: cooldown window (300s) prevented immediate scale-up; consider adding an emergency-attach-failure fast-path that triggers constrained scale-up or immediate fallback routing.
Scheduler placement change: avoid co-locating high-throughput sidecar containers on GPU-serving hosts, prefer separate ingress-dedicated nodes.
resolution_notes: Temporary customer workaround: Lexicon throttled analytics sidecar uploads and rescheduled a nightly validation sweep to off-peak hours. This restored throughput to expected levels.

Short-term platform fixes (rolled to canary 2026-03-12): host-level traffic shaping for sidecar uploader process (tc qdisc policer), scheduler affinity rule change to segregate sidecar traffic from GPU-serving hosts.

Planned medium-term actions: implement a service-level egress QoS for sidecar agents, add sidecar default rate-limits, and create an autoscaler fast-path for attach timeout spikes. Engineering ticket INT-2026-145 created to track these changes.

Follow-ups: (1) Update docs/runbook for customers to limit telemetry concurrency when using dedicated pools. (2) Add detection alert to Console for sudden sidecar upload spikes that overlap with attach latency increase.
final_status: Mitigation deployed to canary; full rollout scheduled
